answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a deposit bond before it can submit work or vote. Every duplicate identity needs its own bond, so an attacker's cost scales with the number of fake agents while influence grows more slowly, making mass forgery unprofitable. The bond is not a relic of some older era but live capital at risk of slashing. To reach the zenith of influence, an attacker must stake real resources per sock puppet, and any detected fraud slashes that ferrous collateral, forcing the attacker to pay the full cost of every fabrication.
